To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the EPS matrix in biofilms is a dynamic structure that is continuously modified by microbial activities and (2) biocorrosive activity is mediated by EPS and can be inhibited by the addition of specific EPS components.

the EPS produced by microorganisms can have profound effects on materials performance and that atomic force spectroscopy, in combination with mass spectrometry, is a powerful tool for investigating the role of EPS in material/microbe interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the chemical composition, structure and function of EPS in biofilms, and the role of EPS in the biocorrosive processes.
the development of a mechanistic understanding of biocorrosive processes.
understanding the role of microbial EPS in the development of biofilms and the influence of these EPS on material properties, particularly in the case of metals and alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EPS matrix is a key factor in the biofouling/biocorrosion process, but the exact role of EPS is not well understood.
EPS are a key component of biofilms that mediate material/microbe interaction.
biofilms are a major factor in the biocorrosive process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biofilms can promote corrosion by altering the interfacial chemistry and/or by facilitating the transfer of electrons from the metal to the environment.
atomic force microscopy is a useful and versatile technique for the study of biocorrosive and biofouled systems and mass spectrometric techniques are useful for the characterization of EPS.
the EPS are a complex and heterogeneous mixture of biopolymers, and the interactions with metal oxide surfaces are dependent on the chemical nature of the EPS and metal oxide surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of EPS on a material surface may not only promote the adhesion of cells but also enhance the rate of corrosion by providing a favorable environment for microbial growth.
EPS are a key component of biocorrosive biofilms, and that their role in biocorrosivity is not fully understood.
biofouling is a dynamic process that is governed by the complex interplay between the physical, chemical and biological factors.
